solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lost name brought to enthral DNA analysis, old chap!

indicators.note: a name that is lost has gone astray, a hint that its letters are jumbled up
analysis breaks things into parts, so the letters of these words are broken down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A name has gone missing, and DNA testing is called in to excite the experts about some old fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NAME, ENTHRAL and DNA are rearranged together; 'Lost' and 'analysis' both point to the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanderthal man is an extinct early human, a very old chap indeed, with the exclamation a playful flourish.

clue.text: Hot flan overcooked very much!

indicators.note: food that is overcooked is ruined and messed about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a hot flan has been badly overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: This British colloquial exclamation is an emphatic yes, meaning extremely or very much indeed.

clue.text: Long-drawn-out course of dinner

parts.note: reads like a tediously slow part of a meal, but means the long passage through the body that food travels along

explanation.definitionFit: The digestive tract is the lengthy path or course every dinner follows through the body.

clue.text: Step out with some fruit

definitions.meaning: to step out with someone is to go out with them romantically
the sweet brown fruit of a palm tree

explanation.definitionFit: To go courting with someone is the verb sense; the palm fruit is the noun sense of the same word.

clue.text: Religious teacher having time to talk

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher of religion is given time to speak to the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is British slang for chatter, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' = talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit on is to talk at length, so the word is a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: On the pitch, stroke young animal with head down, having broken leg joint

indicators.note: the joint is broken open so the other piece sits inside it

parts.note: the hock is the joint in the hind leg of a horse or similar animal

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter, the head, moves down to the bottom of the word

parts.note: a calf is a young cow

explanation.surface: A farmer strokes a calf on the field, but the animal has broken a joint in its leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head down' moves the first letter to the bottom, giving ALFC, and 'having broken' opens the joint around it. In cricket a half-cock shot is played neither fully forward nor back.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-cock is a cricket shot, a stroke made on the pitch that is half forward and half back.

clue.text: Eleventh hour? Surely it starts at 0959!

definitions.meaning: the eleventh hour is the latest possible moment before something is too late
the sixty seconds from 09:59 to 10:00 close out the hour on a clock

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the very latest moment, and literally the final sixty seconds before the hour turns.

clue.text: What might be regarded as analeptic, in toto?

definitions.text: What might be regarded as analeptic, in toto?

indicators.note: suggests the letters, looked at differently, form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pharmacologist ponders what overall effect a stimulant drug has.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ANALEPTIC and IN TOTO make the answer; an analeptic is a stimulant, and a nerve firing is a stimulated response, so the whole clue also hints at the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An action potential is the electrical impulse a stimulated nerve cell fires, which a stimulant could be seen as provoking.

clue.text: Body of writing matter it's a surprise to overlook

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits above, overlooking, the other

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise
pus is the matter from an infected wound

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised that a piece of writing has been overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpus is a whole collection of written texts, a body of writing.

clue.text: Not having a single drum, achieve strike turning round

indicators.note: the turned-round word goes round the other piece, enclosing it
turning signals the word for strike is read backwards

parts.note: to butt is to strike with the head
to win is to achieve or gain

explanation.surface: A drummer tries to win by hitting a beat while spinning around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes TTUB, and 'round' wraps it about the win; 'Not having a single drum' reads as a musician's lament but describes a washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub washing machine has two drums, one to wash and one to spin, rather than a single drum.

clue.text: Well looked after by unorthodox hotel in S Africa

indicators.note: one piece is cared for inside the other, held within it
unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: so, like well, opens a remark: so, what now?

explanation.surface: A guest is well cared for at an unusual hotel in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges HOTEL to LETHO, which holds SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, so it lies in southern Africa.

clue.text: Copy Times tip

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A reader copies a tip from The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the top point or tip of something such as a triangle.

clue.text: Simpleton — in Last of the Summer Wine, favourite in national opinion poll

indicators.note: the second in puts the other pieces inside the poll's letters

parts.note: NOP is the abbreviation of National Opinion Poll, a British polling firm
taken as written

parts.words: Last of the Summer Wine, favourite
parts.note: Compo is the best-loved character from the long-running BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine

explanation.surface: A fool's character from a TV sitcom tops a national popularity survey.
explanation.walkthrough: Last of the Summer Wine was a long-running British TV sitcom about pensioners in Yorkshire, and its scruffy favourite character was a solver's household name; NOP is a British polling firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a foolish, stupid person, a simpleton.

clue.text: The call of the malingerer that comes as a great shock

definitions.meaning: a malingerer, asked if fit for work, might reply that good health never applies

definitions.text: that comes as a great shock

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of astonishment, and also a shirker's claim of never being healthy.

clue.text: More distant-sounding relative

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for more distant is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: farther means more distant

explanation.surface: A relative seems to be growing ever more remote.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is a parent, a close relative.

clue.text: Drunk's break, we hear as an afterthought, from strong drink

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is as spoken, here as slurred speech

parts.note: snap means break, and a drunk would slur it with an sh sound
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A drinker's break is mentioned, almost as an afterthought, in connection with hard liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk saying SNAP slurs it into something like SHNAP, spelt SCHNAP here, then PS is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Chance I'm repairing

indicators.note: repairing means putting back together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone says it is luck that they are fixing the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CHANCE I'M are rearranged; the person repairing is the answer, so the clue doubles as its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic is a person who repairs engines and machines.

clue.text: He's in no rush, parking nice car at side of street

indicators.note: the car is put alongside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, a nice car

explanation.surface: A leisurely driver is parking a luxury car on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking' is a link word: the car is set by the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller walks slowly and in a leisurely way, so is in no hurry.

clue.text: Bearer of oil round Kent and Hampshire as before

parts.note: both counties lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
the same means unchanged, as before

explanation.surface: An oil tanker sails around the coast of two southern English counties as it did before.
explanation.definitionFit: The sesame plant bears seeds pressed to yield a cooking oil.

clue.text: Said to resemble America?

definitions.meaning: playfully, made up of states like the United States

explanation.definitionFit: Stated means declared; whimsically it also means having states, as America does.

clue.text: Ballet performer torn asunder

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer is ripped apart, perhaps by critics.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer.

clue.text: Result in (late in kicking off)

indicators.note: kicking off means making a fuss or brawling, so the letters are thrown around

explanation.surface: A match ends up delayed because play kicked off late.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or bring about as a consequence, to result in.

clue.text: Used ticker

definitions.meaning: the clock hand that ticks round each second

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means previously owned, and also the clock hand counting seconds.

clue.text: Soon to be identified? No!

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for shortly or presently
short for anonymous, an author who is not named

explanation.definitionFit: The word means presently in old English, and is short for anonymous, someone not named.

clue.text: Toy I placed on top of list

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is placed below, so the first sits on top
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I

explanation.surface: A child puts a toy at the top of a wish list.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is a brand of toy plastic building bricks.

clue.text: Spymaster aboard Russian vehicle

parts.note: M is the spymaster in the James Bond stories
someone aboard is in a vehicle
Ivan is a typical Russian name, standing for a Russian

explanation.surface: A spy chief rides with a Russian in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A minivan is a small van, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Simian trained a kelpie

indicators.note: trained means taught new tricks, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: An Australian sheepdog has been taught to act like a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A kelpie is an Australian sheepdog.
explanation.definitionFit: Simian means like or relating to apes and monkeys.

clue.text: Neckwear of cloth

parts.note: reads as fabric neckwear, but the cloth here means the clergy

explanation.definitionFit: The white band worn by priests is neckwear belonging to the cloth, the clergy.
